Chapter 7. Healing, Forgiveness, and the Work of Reclaiming the Self.
Healing's never just a straight path, is it? It's more like a spiral—sometimes you're moving forward, other times you find yourself looping back, and all along, it asks you for patience and care.
When you start reclaiming your voice and your power, that often means coming face-to-face with old wounds, sometimes the kind you haven't looked at in years.
There's a moment that comes after the anger, after all the fighting—a moment when the real work quietly begins. That's the work of forgiveness. And it's not just about letting others off the hook; it's about forgiving yourself.
For the times you stayed quiet. For the times you believed those old lies. For all the ways you learned to make yourself smaller.
Picture someone sitting alone, replaying old conversations in their mind. Maybe you know this feeling. They think about what they wish they'd said, the boundaries they wish they'd set. The regret can feel so heavy. But, little by little, they start to let it go.
They begin to see—everyone's just doing the best they can with what they know. And that's when healing really starts: when you make peace with the past so you can finally move forward.
Most people don't realize just how much strength it takes to forgive yourself. The world? It's quick to judge. Quick to blame. But true change? That begins with compassion. It starts when you decide to treat yourself with the same kindness you so easily give to others.
For some, healing shows up in therapy, or in the pages of a journal, or maybe on long walks with friends. Others find it in rituals—lighting a candle, writing a letter, or just sitting quietly and breathing. There’s no single right way. What matters most is the willingness to show up for yourself—to keep trying, even when it hurts.
As you keep going, it hits you: healing isn't about erasing what's happened. It's about weaving it in—taking the lessons, the scars, and the wisdom, and using all of it to build something new. It's about reclaiming those parts of yourself that felt lost or taken, and learning to love them again.
Forgiveness doesn’t mean forgetting. It means making a choice to move forward, to build a life that feels true. It means not letting old wounds call the shots anymore.
And here's the beautiful thing—as you heal, you light the way for others to do the same.
